The names carried here (SYS, FAN, PSU0, PSU1, ID) are the HIG front-panel LED table's own, in the table's order, which the lamp order matches; the sibling S6301-56STP prints 'PS0'/'PS1' where its table says the same thing, so the printed strings on this device could differ from its table too.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["status-leds"],"wanted":"a straight-on photograph of the left end of the front panel at something better than 5 px/mm.","what":"front-panel-led-legends"},{"note":"'FAN \u25c40' / 'FAN \u25c41' appear at the top of each fan module's right-hand strip in both rear renders and in HIG Figure 5. A photo of the bay with the module out would settle which metal carries the ink.","reason":"needs-hardware","scope":["fans"],"wanted":"photograph of an empty S6301-56ST fan bay.","what":"fan-position-legends"},{"note":"the HIG says 'there are two locations on the case in which the grounding lug may be fixed' and its Figure 23 shows one under a peel-off label on a side wall, but no held source locates it measurably; only the rear location, photographed, is modelled.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["grounding"],"wanted":"a photograph or drawing locating the second lug position.","what":"second-grounding-location"},{"note":"ufispace/fan-402825 states no draw and its own contract records the search: eight UfiSpace datasheets name the part only as an ordering line, with no wattage anywhere near it; this device's HIG likewise dimensions and weighs the fan FRU and tables its LED without a power figure. L29's standing warning is the live count of how much of the chassis total is a floor.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["fans"],"wanted":"a photograph of the fan module's label, or a UfiSpace FRU datasheet.","what":"fru-power-unpublished"},{"note":"the datasheet orders both directions - FAN-402825-HDN / -CDN and PSU-151-DESR / -DISB / -AESR / -AISB - and the HIG says the two are told apart by handle colour, red for front-to-back and blue for back-to-front. The rear render s6301-56st-3-rear.png shows the blue set. Every held component draws only the red exhaust unit, so the back-to-front build can be ordered but cannot be skinned, and no configuration is declared for it rather than declare one that would render identically to the red.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["fans","psus"],"wanted":"blue-handle skins on ufispace/fan-402825, psu-151-dc and psu-151-ac.","what":"intake-airflow-skins-not-drawn"}],"groups":{"fans":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"1+1 - 1+1 hot-swap fans (the device description)"},"index-origin":0,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"ge":{"attrs":{"media":"rj45","speed":"1g"},"description":"the 48 10M/100M/1G RJ45 access ports, ports 0-47; The processor and memory rows carry the vendor's two build grades verbatim ('Standard : Intel Denverton 2-Core @1.6GHz Premium : Intel Denverton 4-Core @1.6GHz'), because collapsing them would state a configuration the vendor does not sell alone.","bottom":"deliberately size-only - no photograph or drawing of the underside exists in the intake. HIG Figure 5 shows top, front and rear only; Figures 12-15 and 27 show the chassis from above and from the front-left; no held image looks at the base. Inventing the label field this class of device usually carries would be a guess. L45's size-only warning stands as the record.","buttons":"drawing - HIG Figure 5's callout 'Reset' points at a single recessed circular button whose centre measures (46.3, 6.2) and whose ring is ~3.3 mm across; drawn with common/reset-button (4 mm recessed pinhole), legend under it. This device has NO Mode button - it has no PoE, so the S6301-56STP's LNK/SPD-vs-PoE lamp toggle does not exist here, and the HIG front-panel LED table lists no mode row.","chassis":"datasheet - 'Chassis (WxDxH) 1RU, 440 x 440 x 43.8 mm', weight 5.62 kg without FRU; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats all three ('S6301-56ST (W x D x H) 440 x 440 x 43.8mm', 'Chassis without FRU 12.39lbs (5.62kg)'). 440 is the body between the ear folds, not a rack face: the HIG Space Clearance section separates 'The S6301-56ST width is 17.32 inches (44.0cm)' from the 'rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', and the brackets ship loose (88 x 43 x 20 mm accessories, 8 M4 screws), so there is no ear extent to subtract. Depth 440 is likewise 'without the field replaceable units (FRUs)'; the HIG says the fan handle projects 25 mm and the PSU handle 38 mm beyond it, and those are carried as relief on the FRU contracts rather than in the chassis depth.","front-layout":"drawing - HIG Figure 5, the front elevation carried under the H = 1.72\" dimension, rendered from the PDF at 600 dpi (page 9). GATE 1: the chassis in it measures 2140 x 214 px, aspect 10.00 against the datasheet's 10.046 (440/43.8) - 0.46% out, so it is orthographic and carries geometry at 4.864 px/mm. Every front number below is measured on that image. The 48 RJ45 jacks sit in four 6-column ganged blocks whose silver shells read directly off the drawing: block left edges 26.32 / 113.91 / 201.29 / 288.67 (three independent steps of 87.59, 87.38, 87.38), block width 84.1, within-block column pitch 13.98 taken from the silver dividers between jacks. The shell band runs y 11.5-36.0 with a continuous silver bar between the rows at y 22.0-24.9; the two 11.0 mm rj45-ganged rows are set inside it at y 12.0 and 24.5, which is the softer axis and is recorded as drawing-constrained rather than measured. The SFP+ block's silver spans x 376.5-434.0 (57.6, four columns on the std 14.25 pitch) with its own centre band at y 20.6-26.1. Vent holes run in two rows from x 84.3 to 436.5, y 2.4-4.6 and 6.0-8.5.","jack-orientation":"drawing+photo - HIG Figure 5's front elevation at 3x zoom, corroborated by the vendor angle render (s6301-56st-1-angle.png): the TOP RJ45 row has its keyway notch UP and the gold contacts toward the centre band (rotate 180 from the std default), the bottom row keyway-down; the SFP+ top row's latch nubs face the centre lamp band (rotate 180), bottom row default. Read from this device's own figure, not carried over from the S6301-56STP, although the two agree.","jack-shells":"drawing+photo - the four 12-port RJ45 blocks and the SFP+ block sit in SILVER ganged shells. Measured on HIG Figure 5 as a grey (max-min < 40, max > 170) mask, which returns the block outlines, the per-jack dividers on the 13.98 pitch and the continuous bar between the rows; corroborated in colour by the vendor angle render s6301-56st-1-angle.png, where the four blocks read light against the dark chassis. std/rj45-ganged and std/sfp-ganged draw the opening only, so each block's shell is a panel.decor fill (#b0b5bb) sized from the measurement, per the s9510-28dc silver-band precedent. Measured here on this device's own figure; the S6301-56STP reached the same construction and its provenance says so, but no number was copied from it.","left-cluster":"drawing - HIG Figure 5 at 4.864 px/mm, with the figure's own callouts naming the three ports top to bottom: 'Mgmt. Port', 'USB', 'Console'. The silver bezel plate measures x 6.4-21.2, y 7.4-38.2, and its two internal silver rails at y 18.3-19.7 and 25.9-27.8 divide it into the three openings the parts are set in. The management and console jacks are drawn with std/rj45-ganged inside the shared plate decor because the plate is one piece of metal - three 16 mm single-port bezels would not fit a 30.8 mm stack. Management jack keyway-up (rotate 180), console keyway-down, both read from the figure's tab notches at 3x zoom. The left-edge network pictogram and the USB / IOIOI legend row under the plate are approximated with the nearest glyphs, as the S9510-28DC does.","lifecycle":"searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S6301-56ST end of life' - no announcement. The vendor still lists the product (ufispace.com S6301-56ST product page) and distributors STORDIS, EPS Global, Pine Networks and Hardware Nation all carry it as current. none-announced is a checked state, not an absence.","port-leds":"drawing - each RJ45 jack carries integrated lamps in the corners of its own aperture (the datasheet's LED row: 'Link and Activity LEDs per port'). std/rj45-ganged draws the opening only and the lamps sit INSIDE the aperture, so they are not drawn - the MX150 and S6301-56STP treatment, recorded on the ge group and in gaps. The SFP+ lamps sit in the centre band between the cage rows, one \u25b2\u25bc pair per column for the upper and lower port, and are drawn with common/sfp-led-pair.","port-numbering":"HIG Port Overview table: 'Port ID 0~47 RJ45 ... 48~55 SFP+', and the printed strip under each column pair reads '\u25b2n n+1\u25bc' - even numbers top row, odd bottom - read at 3x zoom off the front elevation, where '\u25b20 1\u25bc \u25b22 3\u25bc' is legible under the first block. The photographs show no numerals on the ganged shells themselves, so only the strip is modelled.","power":"datasheet gives 'Typical power: 64 Watts (no transceiver)'. The HIG's two Connecting Power sections give the maxima with the testing criteria printed beside them - 45C ambient, optics fully populated, 100% traffic load - hence power-envelope: fully-configured. They differ by input type, not by measure or scope: 'The maximum system power consumption is 111 watts' (DC Version) and 'The maximum system power consumption is 111.5 watts with an input voltage of 100-240V AC' (AC Version). That is two variants of one box, not a source disagreement, so both are carried - power-max-w takes the higher AC figure and power-max-dc-w the DC one. The vendor qualifies all three; nothing here is an unqualified reading.","psu-fru":"ufispace/psu-151-dc@1 and ufispace/psu-151-ac@1 already existed in the library, built from this device's own HIG (Figures 7 and 9, the Component Physical Information table and this same rear render) - their contracts cite the S6301-56ST by name. The rear photographs held here show the DC unit (three screw terminals), which is why the DC build is the base configuration. The fan FRU reuses ufispace/fan-402825@1 (S9510-28DC family): this datasheet orders FAN-402825-HDN where the S9510 orders -HD, same drawn 51.5 x 42.2 face, and the configuration overrides the model attr. Two skin-level deltas on that shared part showed up in the matched-scale comparison against this device's rear render and are recorded rather than fixed: the S6301's fan face is a hexagonal honeycomb grille where the component draws a circular fan aperture, and its status lamp sits low on the right-hand strip where the component draws it top-left. Both belong to the shared component's art, not to this chassis's geometry, and changing them would move every S9510-family device.","rear-layout":"photo-measured - the vendor rear render s6301-56st-4-rear.png (1510 x 151 px, aspect 10.00 vs true 10.046, 0.5% out, 3.432 px/mm), with s6301-56st-3-rear.png (the blue back-to-front variant) as a second reading of the same face and HIG Figure 5's rear strips as a third. Grounding column at the left edge (two M4 holes at (6.8, 7.9) and (6.8, 24.3) with the earth symbol below - one of the HIG's two lug locations, its Figure 24). Fan module faces measured 15.2-66.7 and 67.65-119.15, i.e. width 51.5 exactly as the HIG component table states, on a step of 52.45 recovered by cross-correlating the two identical modules (correlation 0.992) rather than by eye - an eyeball read of the same image gave 51.3 and was wrong. PSU faces measured 322.9-373.4 and 382.9-433.4, width 50.5 against the table's 50.5, step 60.03. The vertical is the softer axis: the fan face reads 39.9 tall against the contract's 42.2 and the PSU face 40.9 against 40.2, so both bays are set to the contract size centred in the 43.8 opening and the difference is recorded here rather than reconciled. Vertical 'PSU0 \u25c4' / 'PSU1 \u25c4' legends sit on the chassis strips right of each bay. The 'FAN \u25c40' / 'FAN \u25c41' texts sit ON the fan modules' own faces in all three sources, not on the chassis, and the shared fan component cannot carry a per-position legend - not modelled, see gaps.","sides":"drawing - HIG Figure 13, which is a genuine side elevation of this chassis with 'Front side' and 'Rear side' labelled and a 220.5 mm dimension on it. The chassis body in it measures 763 x 77 px, aspect 9.91 against the true 10.046, 1.4% out, so it carries geometry at 1.734 px/mm. Two rows of M4 bracket holes at y 9.5 and 34.9; the four mid-chassis holes measure x 226.4 / 252.1 / 277.6 / 303.1, a pitch of 25.5 against the figure's own '1 inch' callout (25.4), and the first of them is where the 220.5 mm dimension lands. The front bracket zone is highlighted in cyan from x 1.2 to 90.0 and the rear zone symmetrically, and the highlight hides the holes inside it, so the three front and three rear hole pairs are placed on the measured 25.4 pitch inside the measured zone and are ESTIMATED, not measured. AXIS CONVENTION: on the RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT; on the LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR (renderer convention), so the left view carries the same pattern mirrored as depth - x - width. The hole pattern is the only content and it is symmetric front-to-rear about the chassis centre, so getting the mirror wrong would be invisible - said here so that the axis is on record as checked rather than as not mattering.","system-leds":"drawing - HIG Figure 5: five lamps, four in a row at y centre 4.73 with x centres 53.77 / 60.45 / 67.23 / 73.92, and a fifth directly under the fourth at y centre 7.20, measured as green blobs on the lit render. That is exactly the five the HIG front-panel LED table defines - SYS, FAN, PSU0, PSU1, ID - and the table's order matches the lamp order left to right. Drawn with common/led-dot (2.0 mm, nearest part) on one centreline; the drawing puts lamp 4 about 0.2 mm lower than its three neighbours, which is noise at this resolution and is aligned rather than copied. States transcribed from the HIG table on each placement. The printed legend strings beside the lamps are below the resolution of every held image - see gaps - so the table's own names are used.","top":"drawing - HIG Figure 5's top view (D and W both dimensioned 440 mm). GATE 1 FAILS on this one: the drawn cover measures 2350 x 2148 px for a square object, 9.4% out, so no absolute scale is taken from it - every position below is a FRACTION of the measured extent multiplied by 440. Four recessed stiffening grooves, centres at y 130.6 / 213.1 / 292.8 / 372.5 from the rear; the two nearer the rear span x 173-389, the two nearer the front x 9-397. The cover screws are placed from the same fractions to about a millimetre. AXIS: y = 0 is the REAR, as the figure is printed - its top edge carries the fan and PSU handles. The figure also puts those fan handles at ITS left, i.e. on the same side as the rear view puts them, so the vendor's top view is laid out to agree with its rear elevation rather than as a true plan; it is transcribed as printed, which is what the S6301-56STP and S9510-28DC top faces do, and this sentence is the record that the handedness was checked rather than assumed. Groove depth is not dimensioned anywhere, drawn as sink decor.","usb-version":"the datasheet says '1 x USB 2 .0 Type-A port' and the HIG's cabling section agrees - 'Connect the USB 2.0 A Type plug'. The accessory list ships a 'USB 3.0 cable', which is the CABLE's rating and not the port's, so the two are not in conflict and no gap is filed. (The sibling S6301-56STP does have a real disagreement here, its datasheet saying USB 1.0; this device's does not.)"},"references":[{"sha256":"ad5db7ca0cc25f5f2f7dce5d1d562f7544cc07195b745de1564371ef8f4dbd37","title":"UfiSpace S6301-56ST L2+/OOB Management Switch Hardware Installation Guide R1.10"}],"version":"1.1.3","views":{"bottom":{"empty":"Searched and not documented: no drawing or photograph of the underside exists in this device's intake. rect.data-members: port-48 port-49 port-50 port-51 port-52 port-53 port-54 port-55

g.data-description: the OOB management jack, HIG Figure 5 callout 'Mgmt. Port', reached by 'the RJ45 OOB port marked a symbol'; its two integrated lamps (HIG Management Port LED table - left green for 1G, right amber for 10M/100M) sit inside this aperture and are not drawn, see gaps
g.title: mgmt

g.data-description: HIG SYS row - Off (no power), Solid Green (Host CPU/BMC boot complete), Solid Amber (power is up but Host CPU boot failed)
g.title: led-sys

g.data-description: HIG FAN row - Off (fans are not initialized), Solid Green (all fans are work normal), Blinking Amber (fan fail: one or more fans need service)
g.title: led-fan

g.data-description: HIG PSU0 row - Solid Green (PSU0 working normal), Blinking Amber (PSU0 fail, PSU0 needs service); the table lists no Off row for the PSU lamps, the dark state exists physically
g.title: led-psu0

g.data-description: HIG PSU1 row - Solid Green (PSU1 working normal), Blinking Amber (PSU1 fail, PSU1 needs service)
g.title: led-psu1

g.data-description: HIG ID row - Off (no power), Blinking Blue (beacon feature is enabled on the switch)
g.title: led-id

g.data-description: the 48 10M/100M/1G RJ45 access ports, ports 0-47; every jack carries integrated link and activity lamps inside its aperture, not drawn (see gaps)
g.title: port-0

g.data-description: the 48 10M/100M/1G RJ45 access ports, ports 0-47; every jack carries integrated link and activity lamps inside its aperture, not drawn (see gaps)
g.title: port-1

g.data-description: the 48 10M/100M/1G RJ45 access ports, ports 0-47; every jack carries integrated link and activity lamps inside its aperture, not drawn (see gaps)
g.title: port-2
